title: How to spot someone / get a good spot on the bench press (and the mistakes to avoid)
summary: NH explains why to get a spot on the bench in commercial gyms (no safeties, poorly placed J-hooks, and the risky roll of shame) and how to ask: state exactly how much help you want on the lift-off and how many reps. For spotters: listen, never jerk the bar out, apply strength gradually, be patient, use an even grip, and take the bar immediately when the lifter asks rather than forcing them to grind.

claims.claim: In commercial gyms bench presses usually lack safeties, so a failed rep must be dealt with without being able to press it up; get a spot.
The 'roll of shame' (rolling the bar down to the hips) is not advisable as a first recourse because it can still be dangerous.

A spotter also provides a lift-off, which matters because commercial racks are often too high (forcing shoulder over-extension) or too low (a half bench before the set), costing strength and tightness and risking shoulder injury.
Just saying 'can you spot me' invites a bad spot; tell the spotter exactly how much help you want and how many reps you're going for, and whether they should touch the bar.
NH wants only a smidgen of help to clear the rack; if the spotter hands him the bar it ruins his setup.
If you say nothing, most spotters will touch the bar during the set.

As a spotter, never jerk or dump the bar out to the lifter: at best you ruin their setup, at worst the bar ends up too far from the shoulders, they lose control and it crashes on the sternum. This happened to NH with 300 lb.
Apply strength gradually on the lift-off, just enough to clear the rack; the lifter should de-rack by extending the elbows, not by pushing with the shoulders.
If you agree to spot, be patient and let the lifter finish; don't grab the bar early because you're in a hurry. You're free to say no.

Spotters should place hands evenly and avoid a mixed grip, since uneven or mixed grips push one side harder and leave the lifter crooked from the start; if you can't get over the bar, spot from the side.
If the lifter asks for help, take the bar immediately instead of yelling 'you got this'; they may be injured. Assisted or forced reps are fine only if requested beforehand.

exercises.name: Bench press (spotting and lift-off)
cues: tell spotter reps and how much help
spotter: even grip, no mixed grip
gradual lift-off, de-rack with elbows not shoulders
exercises.why: safety without safeties and a tight start position
